summary: People call it "original, creative & thought-provoking," and that still lands. It is a crowd-friendly mix of satire, melancholy, and big-concept curiosity that gives a room plenty to talk about without turning into homework.
good_pick_if: You want something smart, funny, and accessible that still feels like a real idea movie.
maybe_skip_if: You want something rougher, stranger, or less polished tonight.

summary: The sell is that "lockdown limbo" feeling: funny, bleak, catchy, and way more formally ambitious than a comedy special usually is. Great for a room that wants something sharp and current-feeling, but not exactly light.
good_pick_if: You want something funny-sad, musically driven, and a little uncomfortably honest.
maybe_skip_if: You want easy laughs or something emotionally lighter than the premise suggests.

summary: People say it "finds heart in chaos," which is basically why it works so well on movie night. It is prickly, funny, and genuinely warm, with family dysfunction that feels affectionate instead of punishing.
good_pick_if: You want something funny, human, and easy to get a whole group on board with.
maybe_skip_if: You want bigger style swings or a movie with less bittersweet family tension.

summary: People describe it as "SO much fun," and that is the right tone to lead with. It is slick, charming, and built around movie-star chemistry, with enough twists and swagger to keep the room smiling.
good_pick_if: You want a stylish, easy-to-root-for con movie with big charisma.
maybe_skip_if: You want something faster, darker, or less rooted in old-school charm.

summary: The appeal is how "sweet" and sad it is at the same time. It has Chaplin slapstick, but the real hook is how gently it turns that physical comedy into something tender and surprisingly emotional.
good_pick_if: You want an older movie that feels warm, funny, and emotionally direct right away.
maybe_skip_if: Silent-era style still feels like homework to your group.

summary: People keep coming back to how "beautiful" it is, which says a lot for a seven-minute Looney Tunes short. The joke is that it is both ridiculously silly and genuinely gorgeous to look at.
good_pick_if: You want a tiny, high-hit-rate palate cleanser with real visual flair.
maybe_skip_if: You need a full feature or want your cartoons less stylized and theatrical.

summary: The surprise is how "more laughs and thrills" still feels true nearly a century later. It plays like a precision-built action comedy, with stunts and visual gags that still read instantly in a room.
good_pick_if: You want an old movie that moves fast and wins people over almost on pure craft.
maybe_skip_if: You want more dialogue, modern pacing, or less silent-era exaggeration.

summary: People call it "absurd, gorgeous," and that is the entry point. It is less about plot than about wandering through a giant visual joke machine and catching more details the longer you sit with it.
good_pick_if: You want something patient, playful, and packed with background jokes for the whole room to notice.
maybe_skip_if: You need a stronger plot engine or comedy that announces every punchline.

summary: If "a deep, meditative reflection of life" inside total sensory chaos sounds good, this is your movie. It is messy on purpose, wildly inventive, and best for a group that wants animation to feel like a dare.
good_pick_if: You want something maximal, strange, and genuinely unlike almost any other animated feature.
maybe_skip_if: You want tonal stability, neat storytelling, or a more family-friendly anime pick.

source_quotes.text: a deep, meditative reflection of life

summary: The appeal is how "breezy" and low-stakes it feels without being slight. It is funny, observant, and quietly affectionate about neighborhood pettiness, family rhythms, and all the nonsense people call communication.
good_pick_if: You want something calm, funny, and deceptively rich without much plot pressure.
maybe_skip_if: You need bigger swings, sharper conflict, or a louder kind of comedy.
